units.en: Fangjian led his followers from Langshan back to Dingzhou and submitted a memorial requesting appointment. The Han founder praised him and at once granted the military commission. He eventually rose to the rank of commissioner and chief councilor.
units.literal: Fangjian led his troops from Langshan back to secure Dingzhou, submitted a memorial requesting orders; the Han founder commended him and at once granted the military commission; he rose in cumulative office to envoy and chief councilor.

units.zh: 太祖受命，加兼侍中。
units.en: When Taizu took the throne, Fangjian was further made concurrent Palace Attendant.
units.literal: When Taizu received the Mandate he was further made concurrent Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 未幾，改華州節度使。
units.en: Before long he was transferred to military governor of Huazhou.
units.literal: Before long he was changed to military governor of Huazhou.

units.zh: 朝廷以其弟行友為定州留後，
units.en: The court appointed his younger brother Xingyou acting regent of Dingzhou,
units.literal: The court made his younger brother Xingyou acting regent of Dingzhou,

units.zh: 〈（《宋史》云：行友上言，偵得契丹離合，願得勁兵三千，乘間平定幽州。
units.en: (The 《Song History》 records: Xingyou memorialized that he had learned of Khitan divisions and alliances and asked for three thousand elite troops to seize an opportunity and pacify Youzhou.
units.literal: (The 《Song History》 says: Xingyou submitted a memorial saying he had detected the Khitans' divisions and unions and wished to have three thousand crack troops to seize an opportunity and pacify Youzhou.

units.zh: 乃移方諫鎮華州，以行友為定州留後。）〉
units.en: Fangjian was therefore transferred to Huazhou, and Xingyou was made acting regent of Dingzhou.)〉
units.literal: Fangjian was therefore moved to govern Huazhou, and Xingyou was made acting regent of Dingzhou.)〉

units.zh: 又以弟議為德州刺史，兄弟子侄職內廷者凡數人。
units.en: His younger brother Yi was also made prefect of Dezhou. Several of his brothers, sons, and nephews held posts in the inner court.
units.literal: His younger brother Yi was also made prefect of Dezhou; brothers, sons, and nephews holding posts in the inner court numbered several men in all.

units.zh: 世宗嗣位，史彥超代之，車駕駐蹕於並門，方諫自華覲於行在，從大駕南巡，以疾就醫於洛下。
units.en: When Shizong succeeded, Shi Yanchao replaced him. The emperor halted at Bing Gate. Fangjian came from Hua to pay his respects at the traveling palace, accompanied the imperial procession south, and sought medical treatment in Luoyang when he fell ill.
units.literal: When Shizong succeeded, Shi Yanchao replaced him; the imperial carriage halted at Bing Gate; Fangjian came from Hua to pay court at the traveling palace, followed the great procession on its southern tour, and because of illness sought medical treatment below Luo.

units.zh: 尋授同州節度使，加兼中書令，未及赴任，以疾卒於洛陽，年六十二。
units.en: He was soon appointed military governor of Tongzhou and further made concurrent Director of the Chancellery. Before he could take up his post he died of illness in Luoyang at the age of sixty-two.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed military governor of Tongzhou and further made concurrent Director of the Chancellery; before he could take up his post he died of illness at Luoyang, aged sixty-two.

units.zh: 輟視朝兩日，詔贈太師。
units.en: Court audiences were suspended for two days. An edict posthumously awarded him the title of Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Court audiences were suspended for two days; an edict posthumously gave him the title of Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 其弟行友繼為定州節度。
units.en: His younger brother Xingyou succeeded him as military governor of Dingzhou.
units.literal: His younger brother Xingyou succeeded him as military governor of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 皇朝乾德中，以其妖妄惑眾，詔毀狼山佛寺，遷其尼朽骨赴京，遣焚於北郊，以行友為諸衛大將軍，自是祅徒遂息焉。
units.en: During the Qiande reign of the Song dynasty, because the cult had deluded the people with false claims, an edict ordered the Langshan Buddhist monastery destroyed. The rotted bones of the nun were transported to the capital and burned in the northern suburbs, and Xingyou was made a general-in-chief of the Palace Guard. From then on the heterodox followers ceased their activities.
units.literal: In the Qiande reign of the imperial dynasty, because the cult deluded the people with false and extravagant claims, an edict ordered the Langshan Buddhist monastery destroyed, the rotted bones of its nun transported to the capital and burned in the northern suburbs, and Xingyou made a general-in-chief of the Palace Guard; from then on the heterodox followers ceased their activities.

units.zh: （《續通鑒長編》：建隆二年八月，義成節度使、同平章事孫行友，在鎮逾八年，而狼山妖尼深意黨益盛。
units.en: (From the Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In the eighth month of the second year of Jianlong, Sun Xingyou, military governor of Yicheng and concurrent Director of the Chancellery, had held his post for more than eight years, while the Langshan sorceress Shenyi and her faction grew ever stronger.
units.literal: (From the Extended Comprehensive Mirror: In the eighth month of the second year of Jianlong, Sun Xingyou, military governor of Yicheng and concurrent Director of the Chancellery, had been in his post for more than eight years, while the Langshan sorceress Shenyi and her faction grew ever stronger.

units.zh: 上初即位，行友不自安，累表乞解官歸山，上不許，行友懼，乃繕治甲兵，將棄其帑，還據山寨以叛。
units.en: When the emperor had just succeeded to the throne, Xingyou felt insecure. He repeatedly memorialized asking to resign and return to the mountains, but the emperor refused. Xingyou grew afraid and began repairing armor and weapons, intending to abandon his treasury, return to a mountain stockade, and rebel.
units.literal: When the emperor had just succeeded to the throne, Xingyou felt insecure; he repeatedly memorialized begging to resign his office and return to the mountains; the emperor did not permit it; Xingyou grew afraid and therefore repaired armor and weapons, intending to abandon his treasury, return to hold a mountain stockade, and rebel.

units.zh: 兵馬都監樂繼能密奏其事，上遣閣門副使武懷節馳騎會鎮、趙之兵，偽稱巡邊，直入定州，行友不之覺。
units.en: The army-and-horse supervisory commissioner Yue Jineng secretly reported the matter. The emperor sent Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate Wu Huaijie riding at speed to join the forces of Zhen and Zhao, falsely claiming a frontier inspection, and entered Dingzhou directly. Xingyou did not detect it.
units.literal: The army-and-horse supervisory commissioner Yue Jineng secretly memorialized about the matter; the emperor sent Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate Wu Huaijie riding at speed to join the forces of Zhen and Zhao, falsely claiming a frontier inspection, and entered Dingzhou directly; Xingyou did not detect it.

units.zh: 既而出詔示之，令舉族歸朝，行友倉皇聽命。
units.en: Then an edict was produced and shown to him, ordering his whole clan to return to court. Xingyou obeyed in panic.
units.literal: Then an edict was produced and shown to him, ordering his whole clan to return to court; Xingyou in panic obeyed.

units.zh: 既至，命侍御史李維嶽即訊得實。
units.en: Once he arrived, Attending Censor Li Weiyue was ordered to question him on the spot, and the facts were established.
units.literal: Once he arrived, Attending Censor Li Weiyue was ordered to question him on the spot and the facts were established.

units.zh: 己酉，制削奪行友官爵，禁錮私第，取尼深意屍，焚之都城西北隅。
units.en: On jiyou day, an imperial order stripped Xingyou of his offices and titles and confined him in his private residence. The corpse of the nun Shenyi was taken and burned in the northwest corner of the capital.
units.literal: On jiyou day, an imperial order stripped Xingyou of his offices and titles, confined him in his private residence, took the corpse of the nun Shenyi, and burned it in the northwest corner of the capital.

units.zh: 行友弟易州刺史方進、侄保塞軍使全暉，皆詣闕待罪，詔釋之。）
units.en: Xingyou's younger brother Fangjin, prefect of Yizhou, and his nephew Quanhui, commissioner of Baosai Army, all came to court to await punishment. An edict pardoned them.)
units.literal: Xingyou's younger brother Fangjin, prefect of Yizhou, and his nephew Quanhui, commissioner of Baosai Army, all came to court to await punishment; an edict pardoned them.)

units.zh: 史臣曰：昔晉之季也，敵騎長驅，中原無主，漢祖雖思拯溺，未果圖南。
units.en: The historian writes: In the last days of Later Jin, enemy horsemen swept deep into the heartland and the Central Plains had no master. Though the Han founder wished to rescue the realm, he had not yet succeeded in marching south.
units.literal: The historian says: In the last days of Jin, enemy horsemen drove deep; the Central Plains had no master; although the Han founder wished to rescue the drowning, he had not yet succeeded in planning the southern campaign.

units.zh: 趙暉首變陜郊，同扶義舉，漢之興也，暉有力焉，命以作藩，斯無愧矣。
units.en: Zhao Hui was the first to rise in the Shaan region and helped launch the righteous cause. In the founding of Later Han he played a vital part. Appointing him to a frontier post was well deserved.
units.literal: Zhao Hui was first to revolt in the Shaan suburbs and together upheld the righteous rising; in the rise of Han, Hui had strength in it; appointing him to govern a frontier circuit—there is no shame in this.

units.zh: 守恩乘時效順，雖有可觀，好利殘民，夫何足貴！
units.en: Shou'en seized the moment to submit to the new dynasty, and there was something admirable in that. Yet he loved profit and harmed the people—what is there to esteem in such a man!
units.literal: Shou'en seized the moment to show loyalty; though there is something to admire, he loved profit and harmed the people—how is he worthy of esteem!

units.zh: 允權、方諫，因版蕩之世，竊屏翰之權，比夫畫雲臺之功臣，何相去之遠也！
units.en: Yunquan and Fangjian exploited a time of chaos to seize frontier power for themselves. Compared with the meritorious ministers whose portraits adorned the Cloud Terrace, how far they fall short!
units.literal: Yunquan and Fangjian, taking advantage of a world in turmoil, usurped the power of frontier bulwarks—compared with the meritorious ministers painted on the Cloud Terrace, how vast is the distance between them!

findings.action: Strip unsupported western date containers from the listed attestations and clear the derived active-date hints. Preserve the relationship, office, death, and honor facts without invented chronology.

findings.action: Remove the unsupported date containers from the listed attestations and clear their derived hints; retain only source-backed dated events already recorded elsewhere.

findings.problem: Sun Fangjian’s AD 944–968 attestation and AD 944–962 active hint use the later Qiande action against Shenyi’s remains as if it were Fangjian’s lifetime activity, although the chapter separately records his death before that reception.
findings.action: Remove the posthumous endpoint from Fangjian’s life attestation and active hint; keep the death claim and preserve any later action as a separately classified posthumous reception rather than life activity.
